title: AI Input Selector
description: AI chat input with a model menu, a separate Effort control, file chips you can drop or paste, a / command menu, and Stop while replying.
api:
| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `models?` | `PromptModel[]` | `built-in` |  |
| `defaultModel?` | `string` | `"Claude Opus 5.5"` | Name of the model selected at first. |
| `placeholder?` | `string` | `"Ask anything. Type / for commands"` |  |
| `headerText?` | `string` | `"Claude Fable 5.1 is free this weekend"` | One line above the box, e.g. a promo. Pass "" to hide the header. |
| `headerAction?` | `string` | `"Try it"` | Label of the header button, which switches to `promotedModel`. |
| `promotedModel?` | `string` | `"Claude Fable 5.1"` | The model the header talks about; its icon leads the header. |
| `onSubmit?` | `(value: string, model: string, options: { /** The effort level, or null for a model without one. */ effort: string \| null; files: File[]; signal: AbortSignal; command: PromptCommand \| null }) => unknown` |  | Sends the message. Return a promise to show the Stop button until it settles; `signal` aborts when the user presses Stop. Without it, the component plays a short pretend reply so the demo feels alive. |
| `commands?` | `PromptCommand[]` | `built-in` | Shown when the message starts with "/". Pass [] to turn the menu off. |
| `onStop?` | `() => void` |  | Called when the user presses Stop while a reply is in progress. |
| `onAttach?` | `(files: FileList \| File[]) => void` |  | Called with the files picked, dropped or pasted into the prompt. |
| `className?` | `string` |  | Extra classes for the root element. |

### PromptModel

| Field | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `name` | `string` |  |
| `description?` | `string` | One line under the name in the menu. |
| `efforts?` | `string[]` | Effort levels, lowest first, e.g. ["Low", "Medium", "High"]. Leave out for a model without a thinking control: the Effort button hides. |
| `defaultEffort?` | `string` | Effort to start on when the model is picked fresh. |

### PromptCommand

| Field | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | `string` |  |
| `label` | `string` |  |
| `description?` | `string` |  |
| `icon?` | `ReactNode` |  |

title: AI Tool Approval
description: Approve or deny an agent's tool calls. Destructive calls need a press and hold, and decided calls fold into a trace with their output.
api:
| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |

| `onRespond?` | `(id: string, approved: boolean, always: boolean) => void` |  | Called when the user allows or denies a call. `always` is true when they chose to stop asking for this tool. |
| `className?` | `string` |  | Extra classes for the root element. |

### ToolCall

| Field | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | `string` |  |
| `tool` | `string` | The tool's name, such as `bash` or `write_file`. Picks the icon. |
| `title` | `string` | What the agent wants to do, in plain words: "Run a command". |
| `input` | `string \| Record<string, string \| number \| boolean>` | A command or text shows as code; an object shows as fields. |
| `reason?` | `string` | Why the agent wants this, shown under the input. |

| `icon?` | `ReactNode` |  |

### ToolCallState

The same states the AI SDK gives a tool part, so a part can be passed straight through: `approval-requested` asks, `approval-responded` runs, and the `output-*` states are the result.

```ts
type ToolCallState = | "approval-requested" | "approval-responded" | "output-available" | "output-denied" | "output-error";
```

title: AI Tool Calls
description: Tool calls inside a chat reply. Each call streams in as one row with a live timer, then they fold into a single line once the answer is ready.
api:

| `prompt?` | `string` |  | The user's message, drawn as a bubble. Only the demo draws one by default. |
| `calls?` | `ToolCallItem[]` |  | The calls in this reply, oldest first. Demo calls when omitted. |
| `answer?` | `ReactNode` |  | The reply under the calls, shown once every call has ended. |
| `className?` | `string` |  | Extra classes for the root element. |

### ToolCallItem

| Field | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | `string` | Stable across renders, e.g. the part's `toolCallId`. |
| `tool` | `string` | The tool's name, such as `web_search`. Picks the icon. |
| `running?` | `string` | While it runs, e.g. "Searching the web". Defaults to the tool's name. |
| `done?` | `string` | Once done, e.g. "Searched the web". Defaults to `running`. |
| `detail?` | `string` | The main argument: a query, a URL, a file. |
| `result?` | `string` | A short result, e.g. "8 results". |
| `state?` | `ToolCallState` | Where the call is. Give every call a state to drive the list from your stream; leave them all out and the calls play through on `duration`. |
| `error?` | `string` | Shown in place of the result when the call fails. |
| `duration?` | `number` | Demo only: how long the call takes, in ms. |
| `icon?` | `ReactNode` |  |

### ToolCallState

The states an AI SDK tool part goes through, so `part.state` can be passed straight in. `output-available`, `output-error` and `output-denied` end a call; the rest show it running.

```ts
type ToolCallState = | "input-streaming" | "input-available" | "approval-requested" | "approval-responded" | "output-available" | "output-error" | "output-denied";
```
